body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.38 (naive base rate 0.45) that: JPMorgan Chase's initial full-year 2027 net interest income guidance (given with Q4 2026 results, Jan 2027) is ≥$110 bn. Evidence: Q3 2026 earnings release (Oct-2026): net revenue $50.9bn (+8%), NII $27.1bn (+13%), NII ex-Markets $24.7bn (+6%); net income $15.3bn; Dimon: 'large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates and geopolitical conditions continue to shift under the surface… we remain prepared for a wide range of outcomes.' SEC XBRL (InterestIncomeExpenseNet, GAAP): Q1 2026 $25.37bn, Q2 $25.51bn, Q3 $27.04bn (9M $77.9bn) vs FY2025 $95.44bn. US 10-yr ~4.9–5.1% (Yahoo ^TNX). Reasoning: Management-tone test: JPM's outlook language is habitually cautious and its January NII guides have tended to sit close to the Q4 run-rate ×4 (history from memory, unverified). Q3 ×4 is ~$108bn; reaching a ≥$110bn guide needs a Q4 step-up plus explicit growth assumptions that Dimon's tone argues against. We lean below base. Resolution: YES if the firmwide (total, managed basis) FY2027 NII outlook in JPM's Q4 2026 earnings presentation/call is ≥$110bn ('~$110bn' or a range with midpoint ≥$110bn counts). If only NII ex-Markets is guided, add the stated Markets NII assumption if given; otherwise void. Source: JPMorgan Chase Q4 2026 earnings presentation / call (jpmorganchase.com IR) and 8-K. Resolve by 2027-01-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Naive: initial guide ≈ Q4 2026 NII ×4; with Q4 likely ~$27–27.5bn, ≥$110bn needs a guide above run-rate — roughly 45%.
